formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the allowance of `spender` over the owner's axl-wstETH (Axelar Wrapped wstETH) to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (ERC20Permit.permit -> _approve).
Uses the owner's current nonce, so any other pending permit with the same nonce becomes invalid.
The signature is valid only until `deadline`; after that, permit reverts with PermitExpired.
An allowance of type(uint256).max is never reduced by transferFrom or burnFrom, so it is unlimited.
formats.shown: Intent 'Authorize spending of tokens', with the spender as a raw address, the max amount in axl-wstETH (or 'Unlimited' at or above 2^255), the expiry date and the owner, under the owner name 'Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0'.

findings.title: Permit metadata.owner names Lido's wstETH, but the contract is Axelar Wrapped wstETH (axl-wstETH).
findings.evidence: descriptor.json metadata: "owner": "Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0". Domain in the same descriptor is "name": "Axelar Wrapped wstETH". meta.json constructorArguments: name "Axelar Wrapped wstETH", symbol "axl-wstETH"; the contract is BurnableMintableCappedERC20, an Axelar gateway token. Case 0 shows owner "Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0" next to "0.5 axl-wstETH".
findings.fix: Set metadata.owner to "Axelar Wrapped wstETH" (or "Axelar"). Optionally rename the file so it does not suggest the Lido wstETH token on Arbitrum.

findings.title: Permit test covers only a finite amount; the 'Unlimited' threshold path is not tested.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json value field: "threshold": "0x8000…", "message": "Unlimited". cases/0.json has only value 500000000000000000, rendered "0.5 axl-wstETH".
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = type(uint256).max that expects "Unlimited".
